name_en: Fuki dawara — rice wrapped in butterbur leaf as a harvest offering
summary_ja: 大豆を炊き込んだご飯をふきの葉で米俵のかたちに包んだ伊賀地域の行事食。田植えの際、田の神に豊作を祈って供えるほか、農作業の合間の携帯食としても食べられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Rice cooked with soybeans is wrapped in butterbur leaves into a small rice-bale shape, an Iga-area harvest offering. It is set before the rice-paddy deity at planting time to pray for a good crop, and doubles as a portable snack for breaks between farm work.

name_en: Chagayu — rice porridge cooked in roasted tea
summary_ja: ほうじ茶などを煎じた茶袋の湯に米を入れて炊いたお粥。耕地が少なく米が貴重だった伊賀地域で、水の量を増やして米を節約する工夫から生まれたとされ、夏は冷やして食べる家庭もあるという。
summary_en: Rice is cooked in water steeped with a bag of roasted tea leaves. Born in Iga, where farmland was scarce and rice precious, the extra water was a way to stretch the grain further; in summer some households chill the porridge before eating.

name_en: Tako meshi — rice cooked together with fresh octopus
summary_ja: 生ダコを調味液とともに米に炊き込む鳥羽市答志島畔蛸の料理。伊勢湾口の速い潮流で身が締まったタコは「潮騒タコ」とも呼ばれ、伊勢神宮の神饌にも用いられるなど古くから身近な食材だったと伝わる。
summary_en: Fresh octopus is cooked directly into the rice with a seasoning liquid, a dish from Adako on Toba's Toshi Island. Octopus firmed by the fast currents at the mouth of Ise Bay is known locally as "shiosai dako," and has long been offered at Ise Shrine's ritual meals as well as eaten at home.
